identity.title: Solvability of the Poisson–Dirichlet problem with interior data in $L^{p'}$-Carleson spaces and its applications to the $L^{p}$-regularity problem
identity.authors: Mihalis Mourgoglou; Bruno Poggi; Xavier Tolsa
identity.journal: Journal of the European Mathematical Society

actual_source_version.comments: 69 pages. To appear in the Journal of the European Mathematical Society
actual_source_version.limitation: Exact pinned author manuscript; publisher PDF unavailable through the normal public link. Differences from publisher text have not been compared.

findings.title: Lorentz estimate uses the boundary dimension
findings.decisive_evidence: For Ω=B1⊂R3,A=I,F=0,Hε=1_Bε, zero-Dirichlet solution at0=ε²/2−ε³/3; L^{1,1}norm∼ε³; ratio diverges. Piecewise radial solution, transmission and boundary conditions verified exactly.
findings.alternative: Not an OCR error: pinned TeX matches. It is not a counterexample to the main theorem, which uses the distinct energy mappings(vii).
findings.impact: False auxiliary uniform estimate; verified main use of bounded compact data and correctly scaled energy estimates survives this counterexample.
findings.repair_status: Scalar L∞ bound with L^{(n+1)/2,1} proved using kernel rearrangement. Full vector-data/energy-membership formulation not certified.

independent_acceptance_check.faithful_source: Definition 2.12(v), source PDF p.21 and author TeX lines 1264-1288; ambient dimension n+1 and adjoint representation retained. A=I makes L=L* in the counterexample.
independent_acceptance_check.all_hypotheses: n=2; smooth connected bounded unit ball in R3; real strongly elliptic A=I; F=0; 0<epsilon<1/2; H=indicator of B_epsilon is bounded, compactly supported and in L^{1,1}. The radial solution is in W_0^{1,2}, continuous with matching radial derivative at epsilon.
independent_acceptance_check.independent_analysis: Inside derivative -r/3 and outside derivative -epsilon^3/(3r^2) agree at epsilon. The radial Laplacian gives -Delta w=1 inside and 0 outside; w(1)=0. w(0)=epsilon^2/2-epsilon^3/3; division by 4*pi*epsilon^3/3 gives 3/(8*pi*epsilon)-1/(4*pi), divergent as epsilon decreases to zero.
independent_acceptance_check.actual_computation: The exact original reviewer script, execution record and result were read and checked against this analytic derivation; their unchanged bytes are reused, not reported as a new execution.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence: Pinned TeX confirms n/2 and n, excluding extraction error. The counterexample does not invalidate existence for bounded compact data.
independent_acceptance_check.core_dependency: Source p.24 Step 2 explicitly uses Definition 2.12(vii), the energy mappings with ambient Sobolev exponents; the false Lorentz uniform bound is not the operative near-pole bound.
independent_acceptance_check.severity_reason: Minor because the verified downstream estimate uses a distinct valid mapping and the false uniform bound is not required for that inference; not because repair is short or because the whole paper survives.
independent_acceptance_check.repair_scope: Only the scalar L^{(n+1)/2,1} to L-infinity estimate follows from the Green kernel rearrangement argument. Vector endpoint and unbounded energy-space assertions remain uncertified.

findings.title: Signed averaging destroys the lower norm equivalence
source_locations: Dyadic lattice normalization and partition convention, PDF p17
findings.decisive_evidence: Normalized half-open boundary squares of geometric side 1/2 and assigned scale 1 satisfy diam(Q)<=ell(Q). An explicit half-space Whitney decomposition gives a common unit cube I; sequence coordinates 1_I and -1_I yield F=0 while both sequence norms for p=q=2 are finite and nonzero, with the N2 squared norm (1/V_Q+1/V_R)/4.
findings.alternative: Absolute-value replacement is sufficient for upper estimates but not lower estimates. Nonnegative sequences suffice for downstream duality and only the upper bound is needed for signed density differences.
findings.impact: The overbroad signed reverse inequalities are false; the inspected duality proof uses nonnegative coordinates and the density proof needs only the upper bound. No invalid core inference depending on the false signed reverse bound was established.
findings.repair_status: Restrict reverse inequalities to coordinatewise nonnegative sequences; retain upper inequalities for all signs by |F(u)|≤F(|u|). Downstream uses explicitly checked.
findings.calculation: acceptance_calculations.json; original independent_checks.json retained as historical support

independent_acceptance_check.faithful_source: Source PDF pp.17,19-20,58-61,63 and author TeX lines 2761-2876: arbitrary signed sequence coordinates are allowed, and F averages their overlapping values.
independent_acceptance_check.initial_report_defect: The old boundary squares had geometric side 1 and assigned scale 1, so diameter sqrt(2)>1 violated the exact dyadic normalization on p.17; closed boundary squares also did not express a disjoint partition.
independent_acceptance_check.correction: At generation j use half-open squares of geometric side 2^(-j-1), assigned ell=2^(-j). Diameter=ell/sqrt(2), area=ell^2/4; nested disjoint dyadic partitions and thin-boundary condition hold. At ell=1 choose Q=[0,1/2)x[0,1/2), R=[1/2,1)x[0,1/2).
independent_acceptance_check.all_hypotheses: Omega=R3_+ is connected, corkscrew, with unbounded 2-Ahlfors regular boundary. Whitney cubes of true side a=2^m tile the slabs [64a,128a] using vertical intervals [ja,(j+1)a], j=64,...,127. Interiors are disjoint and their union covers Omega. For c_hat=1/2, k=3; 32*sqrt(3)*a<64a<=dist(I,boundary)<=127a<256*sqrt(3)*a. I=[0,1]^2x[64,65] has ell(I)=ell(Q)=ell(R)=1 and distance 64 to both boundary cubes, below 512*sqrt(3). Thus I lies in both Whitney regions. The sequence coordinates plus/minus 1_I belong to the required L2 spaces.
independent_acceptance_check.independent_analysis: F=0 exactly. The squared N2 sequence norm is (1/V_Q+1/V_R)/4>0. The C2 sequence functional is positive on Q, bounded locally by 4*(sqrt(V_Q)+sqrt(V_R)), and decays as O(|xi|^-2), since ancestors containing a fixed boundary square and xi have area bounded below by a constant times |xi|^2. Its squared tail is integrable on R2.
independent_acceptance_check.actual_computation: New independently authored SymPy checks executed with exit code 0; exact normalized diameter/area, Whitney inequalities, cancellation, N2 formula and integrable tail recorded in acceptance_calculations.json.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence: For nonnegative coordinates, bounded overlap gives u_Q<=C F(u); for all signs |F(u)|<=F(|u|) retains the upper bounds. Replacing signed coordinates by absolute values cannot justify a lower bound for the original signed averaging map.
independent_acceptance_check.core_dependency: Lemma A.18 p.61 explicitly reduces to nonnegative functions and dual sequence coordinates; the valid restricted inequalities suffice there. Appendix A.3 p.63 needs only the valid upper inequality on signed differences to obtain convergence; the asserted reverse inequality is unused for that conclusion.
independent_acceptance_check.severity_reason: Minor because the false signed reverse inequality is not needed for the inspected core duality/density inferences. This is not a downgrade based on appendix placement or ease of repair.
independent_acceptance_check.repair_scope: Restrict reverse inequalities to coordinatewise nonnegative sequences and retain upper inequalities for arbitrary signs; the corrected counterexample meets the displayed dyadic normalization.

findings.title: Harnack lower comparison omits a sign assumption
findings.decisive_evidence: u=x1 in B2⊂R3, A=I,q=2; average x1²=4/5 while min_B1/2 |u|=0.
findings.alternative: The upper local bound and Hölder statement are not contradicted. Positive Green uses satisfy the necessary sign property.
findings.impact: False overbroad preliminary lower bound, with no demonstrated failure of its positive-solution applications.
findings.repair_status: Fixed-sign requirement is necessary. No claim to reprove full rough-coefficient Harnack theorem or certify all radii/exponents after this necessary restriction.

independent_acceptance_check.faithful_source: Lemma 2.10, PDF p.20 and TeX lines 1235-1244, quantifies over arbitrary weak solutions in W^{1,2}(B*) and any q>0; it has no sign assumption.
independent_acceptance_check.all_hypotheses: Omega=B3 in R3, B=B1, theta=1 so B*=B2 compactly inside Omega, A=I, q=2, u=x1 smooth harmonic and in W^{1,2}(B2).
independent_acceptance_check.independent_analysis: Rotational symmetry or direct integration gives the mean of x1^2 over B_R as R^2/5, hence 4/5 on B2; minimum of |x1| on B1/2 is zero. Thus the lower comparison is false.
independent_acceptance_check.actual_computation: The exact original script and result for the ball moment were checked against the analytic calculation and reused with preserved original attribution.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence: The upper local boundedness/Hölder assertions are not refuted. Fixed sign is a necessary restriction for the Harnack part, not a certification of every displayed radius/exponent after adding that restriction.
independent_acceptance_check.core_dependency: The inspected Harnack comparison on pp.24-25 is applied to a positive Green function away from its pole. The reported sign-changing example does not refute that application.
independent_acceptance_check.severity_reason: Minor because the demonstrated sign-changing failure is absent in the inspected positive-Green dependency, not because the statement is preliminary or easily amended.
independent_acceptance_check.repair_scope: Necessary fixed-sign restriction only; no new proof or wholesale validation of the rough-coefficient Harnack theorem.

The inherited-admissibility interpretation remains possible. No complete admissible counterexample or complete repair was established, so this remains an unresolved request for precise root/packing propagation, not a confirmed error or severity escalation.
